headword: {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}

definitions.explanation: Plants that grow naturally at high altitudes, typically above the tree line. They are adapted to harsh conditions including cold temperatures, strong winds, and intense sunlight.

examples.japanese: {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{咲|さ}いている→咲く：08150_saku⟧。
{高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{採取|さいしゅ}→採取：12901_saishu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。

⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{北|きた}→北：00644_kita⟧アルプス⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{色|いろ}とりどり→色とりどり：10404_irotoridori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しむ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: In the Northern Alps in summer, you can enjoy colorful alpine plants.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{高山|こうざん}→高山：24746_kouzan⟧ (high mountain) and ⟦{植物|しょくぶつ}→植物：03248_shokubutsu⟧ (plants). In Japan, alpine plants are found primarily in mountain ranges such as the Japanese Alps and on mountains in Hokkaido.

Many Japanese {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ} are protected and it is illegal to pick or transplant them. Mountain hikers are expected to stay on trails to avoid damaging them.
